headline: Revenue and profit surge on Viterra scale, guidance raised

drivers.explanation: CEO Greg Heckman cited navigating a complex global environment with agility and disciplined execution, with the expanded (Viterra-integrated) global platform capturing opportunities across the value chain.
Management attributed the gain to strength in the Soybean and Softseed Processing and Refining segments, with volumes up across all four segments following the Viterra integration.
Follows directly from the segment-level results: Soybean adjusted EBIT rose to $445M from $304M and Softseed to $255M from $14M on higher processing volumes and margins.
Fully explained by revenue growth flowing through: gross profit of $1,681M less SG&A of $606M equals $1,075M, versus $738M less $418M a year ago.

Net income growth outweighed a near 50% rise in diluted share count (195M vs 136M) from the Viterra share issuance; GAAP EPS also reflects a larger unfavorable mark-to-market timing swing (-$1.67 vs -$0.69).
Moves with net income and share count on the same basis as diluted EPS; not separately discussed in the release.
Driven by the Soybean and Softseed segment strength described above, partly offset by higher Corporate expenses tied to the addition of Viterra and higher income tax expense on higher pre-tax income.

summary_short: Bunge's Q2 2026 revenue rose 88.3% y/y to $24.04B and net income attributable to Bunge nearly doubled y/y to $678M ($3.47 diluted EPS), driven by Soybean and Softseed Processing volume growth; the company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $9.25-$9.75 from $9.00-$9.50.
summary_long: Revenue rose 88.3% y/y to $24.04B (+10.0% q/q), reflecting Viterra-driven volume growth: Soybean net sales +56% y/y, Softseed +168% y/y, Grain Merchandising +183% y/y. Gross profit more than doubled to $1.68B and operating income (gross profit less SG&A) rose to $1.08B. Net income attributable to Bunge climbed to $678M ($3.47 diluted EPS) from $354M ($2.61) a year ago; adjusted diluted EPS was $2.00 vs $1.31. Bunge completed its $2B Viterra-related buyback program, repurchasing roughly $250M of shares this quarter. Cash fell to $593M from $1,135M at year-end on working-capital build. Bunge raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $9.25-$9.75 from $9.00-$9.50, citing higher Soybean and Softseed results partly offset by lower Grain Merchandising and Milling results.
